questions.question: What is the total amount allocated to the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports in the union budget 2025-2026?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**₹3,794 crore**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Union Budget 2025-2026** was presented in the **Parliament** by the **Union Finance Minister** **Nirmala Sitharaman** on **February 1, 2025**.
 
• In this budget, the **Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports** has been allocated a total amount of **₹3,794 crore** to promote sporting excellence and youth engagement across the **country**.
 
• This allocation is designed to support various initiatives aimed at identifying and nurturing talent at the **grassroots level** through the **National Programme for Development of Sports**.
 
• A substantial portion of the funding is dedicated to the **Khelo India** initiative, which continues to be a cornerstone of India's sports strategy to improve the **medal tally** in international competitions.
 
• The budget emphasizes the development of **sports infrastructure** and the provision of **modern equipment** and **scientific support** to Indian athletes.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Khelo India Scheme**:

 
 
• Launched in **2017-18**, this scheme aims to revive the sports culture in **India** at the grass-root level by building a strong framework for all sports played in the **country** and establishing **India** as a great sporting nation.
 
• The scheme focuses on **12 components**, including playfield development, community coaching development, and state-level **Khelo India Centres**.
 
 
 
• **Sports Authority of India (SAI)**:
 
 
• Established in **1984**, **SAI** is the apex national sports body of **India**, managed by the **Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports**.
 
• It operates various **Regional Centres** and **Academic Institutions** to provide training and high-performance coaching to **elite athletes**.
 
 
 
• **Target Olympic Podium Scheme (TOPS)**:
 
 
• This is a flagship program to provide financial and technical assistance to **India’s top athletes** for the **Olympics** and **Paralympics**.
 
• Under this scheme, the **Ministry** identifies "High Priority" sports and provides customized training under world-class coaches.
 
 
 
• **Mera Yuva Bharat (MY Bharat)**:
 
 
• An autonomous body launched on **October 31, 2023**, to provide an overarching platform for **youth development**.
 
• It serves as a "Phygital" (Physical + Digital) platform to help **youth** realize their aspirations and contribute to the goal of **Viksit Bharat** by **2047**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Youth Population**: India has one of the **largest youth populations** in the **world**, making the budget for the **Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports** critical for **national development**.
 
• **International Events**: The budget allocation for **2025-2026** considers the preparation for upcoming major events such as the **Commonwealth Games** and the **Asian Games** cycles.
 
• **National Sports Development Fund (NSDF)**: The ministry utilizes this fund, established in **1998**, to receive **contributions** from **corporate houses** and **individuals** for the promotion of sports.
 
• **Fit India Movement**: Launched by **Prime Minister Narendra Modi** on **August 29, 2019**, it aims to make fitness an integral part of the daily lives of **Indians**, which is supported by these **budgetary provisions**.

questions.question: As per the Economic Survey 2024-25, during April–September period of financial year 2024-25, the insurance sector attracted about how much percentage Foreign Direct Investment (FDI) into the services sector?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**62%**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• According to the **Economic Survey 2024-25**, the **Services Sector** in India remains a dominant recipient of **Foreign Direct Investment (FDI)**, reflecting the global confidence in the Indian economy.
 
• During the first half of the financial year **2024-25**, specifically the **April to September** period, the **Insurance sector** emerged as a major driver for investment, attracting approximately **62%** of the total FDI equity inflows directed into the **services sector**.
 
• This significant inflow highlights the impact of liberalized policies, where the **Government of India** has permitted higher foreign ownership to strengthen the capital base of domestic insurance companies.
 
• The **Economic Survey** notes that the services sector, encompassing **Finance**, **Banking**, **Insurance**, and **Business Outsourcing**, continues to lead India's growth narrative, contributing substantially to the **Gross Value Added (GVA)**.
 
• The surge in **Insurance FDI** is attributed to the ongoing digital transformation and the increasing demand for life and non-life insurance products across the country. ***Hence, the correct answer is 62%.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **FDI Policy in Insurance:**

 
 
• In **2021**, the Indian government amended the **Insurance Act, 1938**, to increase the **Foreign Direct Investment** limit in the insurance sector from **49% to 74%** under the **automatic route**.
 
• This policy shift was intended to facilitate greater **capital infusion**, improve **insurance penetration**, and enhance the competitive landscape of the Indian insurance market.
 
 
 
• **Economic Survey 2024-25 Overview:**
 
 
• The **Economic Survey** is a flagship document presented by the **Ministry of Finance**, typically a day before the **Union Budget**.
 
• It provides a detailed analysis of the performance of various sectors such as **Agriculture**, **Industry**, and **Services**, while outlining the **GDP growth** projections for the upcoming fiscal year.
 
 
 
• **Insurance Penetration and Density:**
 
 
• **Insurance Penetration** is measured as the percentage of **insurance premiums to GDP**. In India, this figure has been steadily rising toward the **4%** mark, although it remains lower than the global average.
 
• **Insurance Density** refers to the ratio of **premium to total population**, which serves as an indicator of the growth of the insurance business in terms of reach.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **IRDAI and "Insurance for All":**

 
 
• The **Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India (IRDAI)** has set a vision of **"Insurance for All by 2047"**, aiming to ensure that every citizen has appropriate life, health, and property insurance coverage.
 
• Regulatory reforms like **Bima Sugam** (an online marketplace) are being implemented to simplify the process of buying and selling insurance.
 
 
 
• **Role of the Services Sector:**
 
 
• The **Services Sector** accounts for over **50%** of India's **Gross Value Added (GVA)** and is the primary destination for **FDI** inflows into the country.
 
• Sub-sectors like **Computer Software and Hardware**, **Trading**, and **Telecommunications** also contribute significantly to the total **FDI** equity inflows alongside **Financial and Insurance services**.

questions.question: Which legislation enacted in August 2025 provides a regulatory framework for safe online gaming in India and aims to protect citizens from the threat of online money-gaming activities?

options.text: The Online Gaming (Control and Regulation) Bill, 2025
The Internet Safety and Gaming Bill, 2025
The Promotion and Regulation of Online Gaming Bill, 2025

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The Promotion and Regulation of Online Gaming Bill, 2025**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Promotion and Regulation of Online Gaming Bill, 2025** was introduced and enacted in **August 2025** to address the rapidly evolving digital entertainment landscape in **India**.
 
• The primary objective of this legislation is to establish a comprehensive **regulatory framework** that ensures a safe and transparent environment for **online gaming** while curbing illegal **online money-gaming** activities.
 
• It aims to protect **citizens**, particularly the youth and vulnerable sections, from the adverse effects of gaming addiction and the financial risks associated with unregulated **betting** and **gambling** platforms.
 
• The bill mandates the registration of all **online gaming intermediaries** and requires them to adhere to strict **KYC (Know Your Customer)** norms and **age-gating** mechanisms to prevent minors from accessing age-inappropriate content.
 
• It also provides for the creation of an **Online Gaming Regulatory Authority**, which is tasked with overseeing compliance, resolving disputes, and ensuring that games do not violate the **sovereignty** and **integrity** of **India**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Regulatory Context in India:**

 
 
• Before the **2025 Bill**, **online gaming** was primarily governed through amendments to the **Information Technology (Intermediary Guidelines and Digital Media Ethics Code) Rules, 2021**, issued by the **Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY)**.
 
• The **2023 amendments** introduced the concept of **permissible online games** and required the formation of **Self-Regulatory Bodies (SRBs)** to verify games.
 
 
 
• **Taxation and Revenue:**
 
 
• The **GST Council** of **India** decided in its **50th meeting** to impose a uniform **28% GST** on the full face value of bets placed in **online gaming**, **casinos**, and **horse racing**.
 
• This move was aimed at bringing parity in taxation and increasing **government revenue** from the high-growth **gaming sector**.
 
 
 
• **Skill vs. Chance:**
 
 
• Indian jurisprudence traditionally distinguishes between **"Games of Skill"** and **"Games of Chance."** While games of skill are protected under **Article 19(1)(g)** of the **Constitution**, games of chance are often categorized as **gambling** and regulated strictly by **State Legislatures**.
 
• The **Promotion and Regulation of Online Gaming Bill, 2025** seeks to bring a unified **Central law** to provide clarity on these definitions at a national level.
 
 
 
• **Player Protection Measures:**
 
 
• The legislation emphasizes **responsible gaming**, requiring platforms to display warnings about financial risks and time spent, and to provide mechanisms for **self-exclusion** for players showing signs of **addiction**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Economic Impact:** The **Indian online gaming industry** is one of the fastest-growing sectors, with a projected **CAGR** of over **20%**. The **2025 Bill** provides the necessary legal certainty to attract **Foreign Direct Investment (FDI)**.
 
• **Prohibited Content:** The bill strictly prohibits any **online game** that involves **wagering** on the outcome of real-life events or any activity that resembles **money laundering**, as per the **Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA), 2002**.
 
• **Enforcement:** Non-compliance with the provisions of the **Promotion and Regulation of Online Gaming Bill, 2025** can lead to heavy **penalties**, blocking of the **gaming platform** under **Section 69A** of the **IT Act**, and criminal proceedings.

questions.question: Which day is recognised to promote cycling as a sustainable mode of transport internationally and India as well?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**3 june**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **World Bicycle Day** is observed globally on **3 June** every year to recognize the bicycle as a simple, affordable, reliable, clean, and environmentally fit sustainable means of transport.
 
• The **United Nations General Assembly** declared **3 June** as World Bicycle Day in **April 2018**. This decision was the result of an intensive campaign by Professor **Leszek Sibilski** and the support of **56 countries**.
 
• The day aims to encourage **Member States** to devote particular attention to the bicycle in cross-cutting development strategies and to include the bicycle in international, regional, national, and subnational development policies and programmes.
 
• It promotes the use of the bicycle as a means of fostering **sustainable development**, strengthening education, including physical education, for children and young people, promoting health, and preventing disease. ***Hence, the correct option is 3 june.***
 
• In **India**, the day is marked by various **cyclothons** and events organized by the **Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports** and the **Ministry of Health and Family Welfare** to promote the **Fit India Movement**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **12 May:**

 
 
• This date is recognized as **International Nurses Day** worldwide.
 
• It commemorates the birth anniversary of **Florence Nightingale**, the founder of modern nursing.
 
• The day is organized by the **International Council of Nurses (ICN)** to highlight the important role nurses play in health care.
 
 
 
• **13 February:**
 
 
• This day is celebrated as **World Radio Day**, as proclaimed by **UNESCO** in **2011** and adopted by the **UN General Assembly** in **2012**.
 
• In **India**, **13 February** is also observed as **National Women's Day** to mark the birth anniversary of the "Nightingale of India," **Sarojini Naidu**.
 
 
 
• **12 April:**
 
 
• This is the **International Day of Human Space Flight**.
 
• It marks the anniversary of the first human space flight, carried out by **Yuri Gagarin**, a Soviet citizen, in **1961**.
 
• The **United Nations** declared this day to celebrate the beginning of the space era for mankind.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Environmental Impact:** Cycling is a zero-emission mode of transport that helps in reducing **carbon footprints** and combating **climate change**.
 
• **Health Benefits:** Regular cycling reduces the risk of **heart disease**, **stroke**, certain **cancers**, and **diabetes**. It is an effective way to control weight and reduce body fat levels.
 
• **Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs):** Promoting cycling aligns with several **UN SDGs**, including **Goal 3** (Good Health and Well-being), **Goal 11** (Sustainable Cities and Communities), and **Goal 13** (Climate Action).
 
• **Global Participation:** During the **World Bicycle Day 2022**, India set a record for the largest **bicycle rally** organized on a single day across multiple locations to promote physical fitness.

questions.question: Who became the first Indian to receive the prestigious Fred Darrington Sand Master Award in April 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sudarsan Pattnaik**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Renowned Indian sand artist **Sudarsan Pattnaik** made history in **April 2025** by becoming the first Indian to be honored with the prestigious **Fred Darrington Sand Master Award**.
 
• The award ceremony took place in **Weymouth, United Kingdom**, a location globally recognized for its long-standing tradition of sand sculpture art.
 
• This award is named after **Fred Darrington**, who started the tradition of sand modeling in **Weymouth** in the **1920s**, and it is considered one of the highest honors in the world of sand artistry. ***Hence, the statement regarding Sudarsan Pattnaik is correct.***
 
• **Sudarsan Pattnaik** was chosen for this honor based on his decades of contribution to the field of sand art and his ability to combine intricate artistic skill with powerful social and environmental messages.
 
• By receiving this accolade, he has further solidified **India's** position on the global map of contemporary and traditional art forms.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Profile of Sudarsan Pattnaik:**

 
 
• Hailing from the pilgrimage town of **Puri** in **Odisha**, **Sudarsan Pattnaik** is a self-taught artist who started carving sand images on the **Puri beach** at a very young age.
 
• He was awarded the **Padma Shri**, India's fourth-highest civilian award, by the **Government of India** in **2014** for his immense contribution to the arts.
 
• He has represented **India** in more than **60 international sand art championships** and festivals across the globe, winning numerous gold medals and titles for the country.
 
• In **2017**, he created a **Guinness World Record** for building the world’s tallest sandcastle, which stood **48 feet 8 inches** tall on **Puri beach**.
 
 
 
• **About the Other Options:**
 
 
• **Raghunath Mohapatra:** A legendary architect and sculptor from **Odisha** known for his mastery in stone carving. He was a recipient of the **Padma Vibhushan** and served as a member of the **Rajya Sabha**.
 
• **Subodh Gupta:** A contemporary Indian artist based in **New Delhi**, widely known for using everyday objects like **stainless steel tiffins** and milk pails in his large-scale installations.
 
• **M.F. Husain:** Often called the "Picasso of India," **Maqbool Fida Husain** was a founding member of the **Bombay Progressive Artists' Group** and is one of the most celebrated painters in Indian history.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Global Impact:** Pattnaik is known for using his art to raise awareness about global issues such as **Global Warming**, **COVID-19 safety**, **plastic pollution**, and world peace.
 
• **Educational Contribution:** He established the **Sudarsan Sand Art Institute** in **Puri** to provide professional training to aspiring sand artists, ensuring the continuity of this unique art form in **India**.
 
• **Cultural Diplomacy:** His participation in events like the **International Sand Sculpting Championship** in the **USA**, **Russia**, and **Japan** serves as a form of cultural diplomacy, showcasing Indian talent and heritage to an international audience.

questions.question: In which country did the Indian Army participate in the multinational peacekeeping Exercise Khaan Quest 2025 held in June 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mongolia**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Indian Army** participated in the multinational peacekeeping exercise **Khaan Quest 2025**, which was hosted in **Mongolia** during **June 2025**.
 
• Exercise **Khaan Quest** is an annual event co-sponsored by the **Mongolian Armed Forces (MAF)** and the **United States Indo-Pacific Command (USINDOPACOM)**.
 
• The primary objective of the exercise is to enhance the **interoperability** of the participating nations and to train their personnel for **United Nations Peacekeeping Operations (UNPKO)**.
 
• In the **2025** iteration, the **Indian Army** contingent, often comprising personnel from specialized infantry units like the **GARHWAL RIFLES** or **GORKHA RIFLES**, engaged in various tactical drills and humanitarian assistance scenarios.
 
• The exercise involves approximately **20 countries**, providing a platform for sharing best practices and developing professional relationships between military forces from across the globe. ***Hence, the correct answer is Mongolia.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **History of Khaan Quest:**

 
 
• The exercise began as a **bilateral** event between the **USA** and **Mongolia** in the year **2003**.
 
• It transitioned into a **multinational** peacekeeping exercise in **2006**, allowing more nations to participate and contribute to global security.
 
 
 
• **Geographical Context:**
 
 
• The training is traditionally conducted at the **Five Hills Training Area**, located near the Mongolian capital, **Ulaanbaatar**.
 
• **Mongolia**, known as the "Land of the Eternal Blue Sky," provides a rugged and challenging terrain that is ideal for simulating diverse peacekeeping environments.
 
 
 
• **Indo-Mongolian Defense Ties:**
 
 
• Apart from **Khaan Quest**, **India** and **Mongolia** conduct a bilateral military exercise named **Nomadic Elephant**, which focuses on counter-terrorism and mountain warfare.
 
• India considers **Mongolia** a "**Spiritual Neighbour**" and a key partner in its **Act East Policy**.
 
 
 
• **Significance for India:**
 
 
• Participation in such exercises allows the **Indian Army** to demonstrate its vast experience in **UN Missions**, as India is one of the largest **troop-contributing countries** to the **United Nations**.
 
• It strengthens diplomatic and military cooperation with **Central Asian** and **East Asian** nations.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Exercise Components:** The training usually includes a **Command Post Exercise (CPX)** for staff officers and a **Field Training Exercise (FTX)** for troops on the ground.
 
• **Focus Areas:** The curriculum includes **Combat Medical Care**, **Cordon and Search** operations, **Convoy Protection**, and **IED (Improvised Explosive Device)** awareness.
 
• **UN Standards:** All activities are designed according to the **United Nations** training standards to ensure readiness for deployment in volatile regions under the **UN Charter**.
 
• **Global Participation:** Nations such as **Canada**, **Germany**, **South Korea**, **Japan**, and **Vietnam** have been regular participants in previous editions alongside **India**.

questions.question: Which among the following organisations released the Supervisory Data Quality Index (sDQI) report in March 2025?

options.text: Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI)

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Reserve Bank of India (RBI)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Reserve Bank of India (RBI)** released the **Supervisory Data Quality Index (sDQI)** report in **March 2025** to enhance the quality of returns submitted by various financial institutions.
 
• The **sDQI** is a performance metric designed to evaluate the **data quality** of **Supervised Entities (SEs)**, which includes **Scheduled Commercial Banks**, **Non-Banking Financial Companies (NBFCs)**, and **Urban Cooperative Banks (UCBs)**.
 
• The index assesses data based on four pillars: **accuracy**, **consistency**, **completeness**, and **timeliness**. This ensures that the data used for regulatory oversight is reliable and robust.
 
• This initiative is part of the **RBI's** broader strategy to transition towards **data-driven supervision** and improve the **Risk-Based Supervision (RBS)** framework.
 
• By monitoring the **sDQI**, the **central bank** aims to provide feedback to **Supervised Entities**, encouraging them to strengthen their internal **data management systems** and reduce reporting errors.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Reserve Bank of India (RBI):**

 
 
• It was established on **April 1, 1935**, under the provisions of the **Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934**, following the recommendations of the **Hilton Young Commission**.
 
• The **RBI** was **nationalized** on **January 1, 1949**, and it serves as the **Central Bank** of the country, headquartered in **Mumbai**.
 
• Its primary functions include **monetary policy** formulation, **currency issuance**, regulation of the **banking system**, and managing **foreign exchange reserves**.
 
 
 
• **Regulatory Tools and Systems:**
 
 
• The **RBI** utilizes **DAKSHA**, an advanced supervisory monitoring system, to automate reporting processes and facilitate seamless data exchange between the regulator and the **SEs**.
 
• Another important index released by the **RBI** is the **Financial Inclusion Index (FI-Index)**, which captures the extent of **financial inclusion** across **India** based on three parameters: **Access**, **Usage**, and **Quality**.
 
 
 
• **Other Organizations mentioned:**
 
 
• **Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI):** Established in **1988** (statutory status in **1992**), it regulates the **securities and capital markets** in **India**.
 
• **National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI):** An umbrella organization for operating retail payments and settlement systems like **UPI**, **IMPS**, and **RuPay**.
 
• **State Bank of India (SBI):** The largest **public sector bank** in **India**, formed in **1955** after the nationalization of the **Imperial Bank of India**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The **Supervisory Data Quality Index** helps in identifying systemic risks at an early stage by ensuring that the **micro-level data** submitted by banks is free from discrepancies.
 
• It fosters a culture of **transparency** and **accountability** within the **financial sector**, as **Supervised Entities** are ranked based on their compliance with **reporting standards**.
 
• The implementation of **sDQI** aligns with **global best practices** in central banking supervision, particularly those recommended by the **Basel Committee on Banking Supervision (BCBS)**.

questions.question: Menar, one of the newly added wetlands to Ramsar sites, is located in which state?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Rajasthan**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Menar** is located in the **Udaipur district** of the state of **Rajasthan**. It has gained international recognition for its rich biodiversity and community-led conservation efforts.
 
• It is famously known as the **"Bird Village"** of **Rajasthan** because it serves as a major habitat for a wide variety of migratory and resident bird species.
 
• The wetland consists of two primary seasonal lakes, namely **Brahma Lake** and **Dhandh Lake**, which spread across approximately **400 hectares** of land.
 
• In **2022**, the **Rajasthan** state government initiated the formal process to declare Menar as a **Ramsar site**, seeking to provide it with international protection under the **Ramsar Convention**.
 
• The conservation of this wetland is unique because it is entirely managed by the local **Menaria community**, who have protected the ecosystem for centuries without formal government intervention until recently.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Ramsar Convention:**

 
 
• The **Ramsar Convention** on Wetlands is an intergovernmental treaty established in **1971** in the city of **Ramsar, Iran**.
 
• It provides the framework for national action and international cooperation for the conservation and wise use of **wetlands** and their resources.
 
• India became a signatory to this convention on **February 1, 1982**.
 
 
 
• **Wetlands in Rajasthan:**
 
 
• Currently, **Rajasthan** is home to two prominent **Ramsar sites**: **Keoladeo National Park** (designated in **1981**) in **Bharatpur** and **Sambhar Lake** (designated in **1990**) in **Jaipur**.
 
• Menar is slated to become the **third Ramsar site** in the state, boosting eco-tourism and conservation funding in the **Mewar region**.
 
 
 
• **Biodiversity at Menar:**
 
 
• The village attracts more than **150 species** of birds every year during the winter season.
 
• Key species include the **Greater Flamingo**, **Great White Pelican**, **Bar-headed Goose**, **Northern Shoveler**, and the **Common Crane**.
 
• The presence of these birds indicates a healthy aquatic ecosystem, which the **local villagers** maintain by prohibiting fishing and harmful agricultural runoff.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Community Conservation Model:** The **Menaria community** has set a global example by voluntarily banning fishing, sand mining, and the use of chemical fertilizers near the lakes to ensure the safety of the birds.
 
• **Legal Status:** The area was notified as a **Wetland** under the **Wetland (Conservation and Management) Rules, 2017**, which provides a legal shield against encroachment and pollution.
 
• **National Context:** As of **August 2024**, **India** has a total of **85 Ramsar sites**, covering an area of over **1.3 million hectares**. **Tamil Nadu** currently holds the highest number of sites (**18**), followed by **Uttar Pradesh** (**10**).
 
• **Significance of Wetlands:** Often referred to as the **"Kidneys of the Landscape,"** wetlands like Menar play a crucial role in **groundwater recharge**, carbon sequestration, and flood control.

questions.question: Which of the following Government of India initiatives focuses on advancing research and development in emerging areas such as quantum computing, communication, and sensing with a budget outlay of around ₹6,000 crore for 2023–2031?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**National Quantum Mission (NQM)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Union Cabinet, chaired by **Prime Minister Narendra Modi**, approved the **National Quantum Mission (NQM)** on **April 19, 2023**.
 
• The mission has a total financial outlay of **₹6,003.65 crore** and is scheduled to span from the financial year **2023-24** to **2030-31**.
 
• The primary objective of the mission is to seed, nurture, and scale up scientific and industrial **Research and Development (R&D)** and create a vibrant ecosystem in **Quantum Technology (QT)**.
 
• It focuses on four major thematic areas: **Quantum Computing**, **Quantum Communication**, **Quantum Sensing and Metrology**, and **Quantum Materials and Devices**.
 
• The mission aims to develop intermediate-scale quantum computers with **50-1000 physical qubits** within **8 years** using various platforms like superconducting and photonic technology.
 
• It is implemented by the **Department of Science & Technology (DST)** under the **Ministry of Science & Technology**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **National Supercomputing Mission (NSM):**

 
 
• Launched in **2015** with an estimated cost of **₹4,500 crore**, this mission aims to empower national academic and R&D institutions by installing a vast supercomputing grid.
 
• It is jointly steered by the **Department of Science and Technology (DST)** and the **Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY)**.
 
 
 
• **National Nanotechnology Mission (Nano Mission):**
 
 
• Launched in **May 2007** as an umbrella programme for the capacity building and promotion of **nanotechnology** in India.
 
• It focuses on basic research, infrastructure development, and promoting **public-private partnerships** in the nano-science sector.
 
 
 
• **Digital India Mission:**
 
 
• Launched on **July 1, 2015**, this campaign aims to ensure that government services are made available to citizens electronically by improving online infrastructure.
 
• It encompasses various initiatives such as **BharatNet**, **e-Sign**, and **National Scholarship Portal** to transform India into a digitally empowered society.
 
 
 
• **Quantum Communication Targets:**
 
 
• The **NQM** specifically targets **satellite-based secure quantum communications** between ground stations over a range of **2,000 kilometers** within India and long-distance secure quantum communications with other countries.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• With the launch of this mission, **India** became the **seventh country** in the world to have a dedicated quantum mission, joining the ranks of the **USA**, **China**, **France**, **Austria**, **Finland**, and **Canada**.
 
• The mission will establish four **Thematic Hubs (T-Hubs)** in top academic and National R&D institutes to promote fundamental research and translational work.
 
• Quantum technology utilizes the principles of **quantum mechanics**, such as **superposition** and **entanglement**, to perform calculations and tasks that are impossible for classical computers.
 
• This initiative is expected to benefit sectors like **Communication**, **Health**, **Financial**, **Energy**, **Drug Design**, and **Space Applications**.

questions.question: According to the the Sustainable Development Report 2025, what is the percentage of the population with access to electricity in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**99.2%**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• According to the **Sustainable Development Report 2025**, **India** has achieved a significant milestone in energy accessibility, with **99.2%** of its population having access to **electricity**.
 
• The report is a comprehensive assessment of progress made by **United Nations** member states towards achieving the **17 Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs)**, specifically highlighting **SDG 7** (Affordable and Clean Energy).
 
• This high percentage reflects the culmination of various large-scale infrastructure projects aimed at **rural electrification** and last-mile connectivity across **28 states** and **8 Union Territories**.
 
• The **Sustainable Development Solutions Network (SDSN)**, which prepares this report, utilizes data from various international and national sources to track the **SDR Index** and individual **SDG Dashboards**.
 
• Achieving **99.2%** electrification is a critical indicator of **socio-economic development**, as it directly impacts **education**, **healthcare**, and **industrial productivity** in both **urban** and **rural areas**. ***Hence, the correct answer is 99.2%.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Sustainable Development Goal 7 (SDG 7):**

 
 
• This goal aims to ensure access to **affordable, reliable, sustainable, and modern energy** for all by the **year 2030**.
 
• India’s progress in this sector is monitored through indicators like **access to electricity** and **access to clean fuels and technologies for cooking**.
 
 
 
• **Pradhan Mantri Sahaj Bijli Har Ghar Yojana (Saubhagya):**
 
 
• Launched in **September 2017**, the **Saubhagya scheme** was designed to provide **free electricity connections** to all un-electrified households in **rural areas** and poor households in **urban areas**.
 
• It has been a major driver in pushing the national electrification rate towards the **99.2%** mark mentioned in the **2025 report**.
 
 
 
• **Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Gram Jyoti Yojana (DDUGJY):**
 
 
• Launched in **2014**, this scheme focused on **feeder separation**, strengthening of **sub-transmission and distribution networks**, and **metering** at all levels in **rural India**.
 
• It laid the foundational infrastructure necessary for the **Sustainable Development Report's** recorded growth in **electricity access**.
 
 
 
• **Sustainable Development Solutions Network (SDSN):**
 
 
• Operates under the auspices of the **UN Secretary-General** and is led by **Jeffrey Sachs**.
 
• The annual **Sustainable Development Report** provides the **SDG Index**, which ranks countries based on their overall performance across all **17 goals**.
 
• In the **2025** data context, the report emphasizes the transition from **fossil fuels** to **renewable energy** alongside universal **grid connectivity**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The transition from **partial electrification** to **99.2% access** involved integrating **off-grid** and **decentralized renewable energy** solutions in remote **hilly** and **tribal regions**.
 
• While **access to electricity** has reached **99.2%**, the **2025 report** also monitors the **reliability** of power supply, measured in **hours of supply per day**.
 
• The **International Energy Agency (IEA)** and the **World Bank** are key data contributors to the **SDSN** for validating global **energy statistics**.
 
• The **Ministry of Power** in **India** reported the completion of **100% village electrification** in **April 2018**, which paved the way for the high **household-level** access rates seen in current reports.

questions.question: When was the Pan‑India Fire Safety Week observed by the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare in April 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**April 21–25**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Ministry of Health and Family Welfare (MoHFW)** organized the **Pan-India Fire Safety Week** from **April 21 to April 25, 2025**. This initiative was specifically designed to bolster fire prevention mechanisms across all healthcare institutions in the country.
 
• The primary objective of this week was to **sensitize healthcare staff**, including doctors, nurses, and administrative personnel, about the critical nature of fire safety in a clinical environment where patients may be non-ambulatory or vulnerable.
 
• During this period, the **Government of India** directed all **Central Government Hospitals** and **AIIMS** institutions to conduct rigorous **Fire Safety Audits** and **Electrical Load Audits** to prevent short circuits, which are a leading cause of hospital fires.
 
• The observance involved comprehensive **mock drills** conducted in coordination with local **Fire Departments**. These drills simulated emergency evacuation procedures and the effective use of **fire extinguishers** and **hydrant systems**.
 
• Special emphasis was placed on the safety of **Oxygen Plants** and **ICUs (Intensive Care Units)**, ensuring that all life-saving equipment is protected against potential fire hazards through strictly enforced **Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs)**. ***Hence, the correct answer is April 21–25.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **National Fire Service Day:**

 
 
• In **India**, **National Fire Service Day** is observed annually on **April 14**.
 
• It commemorates the brave firemen who lost their lives during the **Victoria Dock explosion** in **Bombay** (now Mumbai) on **April 14, 1944**.
 
• The **Ministry of Home Affairs** typically extends this observance into a **Fire Service Week** (usually **April 14–20**), which serves as a precursor to specialized departmental weeks like the one held by the **Health Ministry**.
 
 
 
• **Regulatory Framework:**
 
 
• Fire safety standards in India are governed by the **National Building Code (NBC) 2016**, specifically **Part IV**, which deals with Fire and Life Safety.
 
• Healthcare facilities are classified as **Institutional Buildings** under the code, requiring stringent fire-resistant construction and **Clearance Certificates (NOC)** from the **Fire Service Department**.
 
 
 
• **NDMA Guidelines:**
 
 
• The **National Disaster Management Authority (NDMA)** provides specific guidelines for **Hospital Safety**, emphasizing the need for **disaster management plans** and regular training of "fire marshals" within hospital staff.
 
• These guidelines highlight the importance of **smoke detectors**, **automatic sprinkler systems**, and clearly marked **fire exits** that must remain unobstructed at all times.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Causes of Hospital Fires:** Statistics indicate that nearly **75%** of hospital fires in **India** are caused by **electrical short circuits**, often due to overloaded circuits in aging infrastructure or high-power medical machinery.
 
• **Training and Awareness:** The **MoHFW** 2025 initiative mandated that at least **80%** of the on-duty staff at any given time must be trained in basic **firefighting techniques** and **patient evacuation protocols**.
 
• **Reporting Mechanism:** Following the **Fire Safety Week**, all medical superintendents were required to submit a **compliance report** to the **Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS)** confirming the functional status of their fire-fighting equipment.

questions.question: How long was the planned duration of the Ax‑4 mission aboard the ISS?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**14–21 days**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Axiom Mission 4 (Ax-4)** is the fourth planned private astronaut mission to the **International Space Station (ISS)**, managed by the private **American** company **Axiom Space**.
 
• The mission is scheduled to have a total duration of approximately **14–21 days**, which includes the time required for travel, docking, and the **14-day** stay at the orbiting laboratory for conducting scientific research. ***Hence, the correct answer is 14–21 days.***
 
• This mission is a landmark event for the **Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO)**, as it involves the participation of an **Indian Gaganyaatri** (astronaut) in a joint mission with **NASA**.
 
• **Group Captain Shubhanshu Shukla** has been identified as the primary astronaut from **India** for the **Ax-4** mission, while **Group Captain Prasanth Balakrishnan Nair** has been named as the backup.
 
• The mission utilizes the **SpaceX Dragon** spacecraft and is launched via the **Falcon 9** rocket from the **Kennedy Space Center** in **Florida, USA**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **International Collaboration:**

 
 
• The **Ax-4** mission is a result of a bilateral agreement between **India** and the **United States**, solidified during **Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s** state visit to the **USA** in **June 2023**.
 
• The collaboration falls under the **iCET (Initiative on Critical and Emerging Technology)** framework, aimed at enhancing cooperation in space exploration and high-end technology.
 
 
 
• **The Crew Members:**
 
 
• The mission is commanded by **Peggy Whitson**, a veteran **NASA** astronaut and the **Axiom Space** Director of Human Spaceflight, who holds the record for the most cumulative time spent in space by an **American**.
 
• Other crew members include **Sławosz Uznański** from **Poland** (representing the **European Space Agency**) and **Tibor Kapu** from **Hungary**, making it a truly multi-national expedition.
 
 
 
• **Training and Preparation:**
 
 
• The **Indian** astronauts selected for this mission undergo rigorous training at **NASA's Johnson Space Center** in **Houston, Texas**.
 
• The training includes **ISS** system operations, emergency protocols, microgravity adaptation, and specific payload handling related to the scientific experiments planned for the **14–21 days** duration.
 
 
 
• **Historical Context:**
 
 
• This mission marks the return of an **Indian** citizen to space after a gap of several decades. The first **Indian** in space was **Wing Commander Rakesh Sharma**, who flew to the **Soviet Salyut 7** space station in **1984**.
 
• While **Indian-origin** astronauts like **Kalpana Chawla** and **Sunita Williams** have flown with **NASA**, **Shubhanshu Shukla** represents the official **Indian** space program’s push toward the **Gaganyaan** mission goals.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Mission Significance:** The **Ax-4** mission serves as a precursor to **India’s** own human spaceflight program, **Gaganyaan**, by providing **ISRO** with valuable experience in international docking standards and **ISS** operations.
 
• **Scientific Objectives:** During their stay, the crew will perform approximately **25+** different **experiments** focusing on human health, biology, and physical sciences in a microgravity environment.
 
• **Axiom Space's Vision:** Axiom Space aims to build the **Axiom Station**, the world’s first commercial space station, which will eventually detach from the **ISS** to operate independently.

questions.question: Who is the recipient of the 2025 PSA Women’s Young Player of the Season Award?

questions.question: Which of the following countries hosted the AI Action Summit 2025 held in February 2025?
questions.solution:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **AI Action Summit 2025** was officially hosted by **France** in the city of **Paris** on **February 10th and 11th, 2025**.
 
• This summit represents the third major international gathering focused on **Artificial Intelligence (AI)** governance, succeeding the **Bletchley Park Summit** in the **United Kingdom** (**2023**) and the **Seoul AI Summit** in **South Korea** (**2024**).
 
• The primary objective of the **Paris Summit** was to transition from high-level safety discussions to **concrete global actions**, focusing on the public interest, **economic impact**, and the ethical deployment of AI technologies.
 
• It brought together **Heads of State**, representatives from international organizations, **civil society leaders**, and executives from leading AI companies like **OpenAI**, **Google DeepMind**, and **Mistral AI**.
 
• The summit aimed to foster international cooperation to mitigate risks such as **misinformation**, **deepfakes**, and threats to **cybersecurity** while promoting **innovation** and **economic growth**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Evolution of AI Summits:**
 
 
• **Bletchley Park (2023):** The inaugural event that produced the **Bletchley Declaration**, establishing a global consensus on the need to manage "frontier" AI risks.
 
• **Seoul Summit (2024):** This summit expanded the focus to the three pillars of **Safety, Innovation, and Inclusivity**, ensuring that AI development is not restricted to a few wealthy nations.
 
 
 
• **Key Themes in Paris:** 
 
 
• The **AI Action Summit** emphasized "AI for the Planet," "AI for Public Interest," and "AI for Work," addressing how automation will redefine the **global labor market**.
 
• Discussions also prioritized **Culture and Media**, looking at how AI impacts **intellectual property** and **creative industries**.
 
 
 
• **Global Governance Frameworks:**
 
 
• The summit supported the ongoing work of the **United Nations (UN)** and the **OECD** in creating standardized **regulatory frameworks**.
 
• It sought to strengthen the network of **AI Safety Institutes** (AISIs) across different countries to share technical expertise and safety testing protocols.
 
 
 
• **Host Country Ambitions:**
 
 
• By hosting the event, **France**, under President **Emmanuel Macron**, aimed to position itself as a central hub for **AI research** and **European technological sovereignty**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Democratic Participation:** A unique aspect of the **Paris** summit was the involvement of **civil society** and **academic researchers** to ensure that AI development aligns with **human rights** and **democratic values**.
 
• **Access to Computing Power:** One of the critical debates involved the democratization of **compute resources** (high-performance hardware), aiming to prevent a **digital divide** between the **Global North** and the **Global South**.
 
• **Safety Standards:** The summit reinforced the commitment to **pre-deployment testing** for the most powerful AI models to prevent catastrophic risks associated with **autonomous systems**.
 
• **Paris AI Network:** The event encouraged the formation of international partnerships to develop **open-source AI** models that are transparent and accessible to the global community.

questions.question: Which of the following specific subgroup receives treatment for diarrhoea under the Stop Diarrhoea Campaign launched in June/July 2025?

options.text: Children under five suffering from diarrhoea
Rural children above six years with diarrhoea

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Children under five suffering from diarrhoea**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Stop Diarrhoea Campaign** was strategically launched to address the critical issue of child mortality, specifically targeting **children under five years of age**. This demographic is most vulnerable to the dehydrating effects of diarrhoeal diseases.
 
• In **June/July 2024** (with cycles continuing into **2025**), the **Union Ministry of Health and Family Welfare** rebranded the existing **Intensified Diarrhoea Control Fortnight (IDCF)** into a more comprehensive **two-month-long campaign**.
 
• The primary objective of the campaign is **"Zero Childhood Diarrhoea Deaths,"** emphasizing that no child should lose their life to a preventable and treatable condition like diarrhoea.
 
• The campaign involves the distribution of **ORS (Oral Rehydration Salts)** and **Zinc tablets** to families with **children under five**. While **ORS** helps in immediate rehydration, **Zinc** reduces the duration and severity of the episode. ***Hence, the specific subgroup receiving treatment is children under five.***
 
• The **Union Health Minister**, **Shri J.P. Nadda**, highlighted the shift from a **14-day** strategy to a **60-day** intensive program to ensure wider reach and better health outcomes across the country.

• **Diarrhoea and Child Mortality:** Diarrhoea remains a leading cause of death among **children under five** globally and in **India**. It results in severe dehydration and loss of essential minerals, which can be fatal if not managed timely with **rehydration therapy**.
 
• **Role of Frontline Workers:** **ASHA (Accredited Social Health Activist)** workers play a pivotal role in this campaign by conducting **house-to-house visits** to distribute **ORS** packets and educate mothers about **infant and young child feeding (IYCF)** practices.
 
• **ORS and Zinc Combination:** The **World Health Organization (WHO)** recommends the use of **low-osmolarity ORS** and **Zinc supplementation** for **14 days** as the gold standard for treating childhood diarrhoea. **Zinc** not only treats the current episode but also prevents future episodes for the next **2 to 3 months**.
 
• **NFHS-5 Data:** According to the **National Family Health Survey (NFHS-5)**, while there has been an improvement in the usage of **ORS**, awareness regarding the importance of **Zinc** therapy still needs significant enhancement among rural and urban populations.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **WASH Initiatives:** The campaign is closely linked with **WASH (Water, Sanitation, and Hygiene)** goals. It encourages **handwashing with soap**, the use of **safe drinking water**, and the **hygienic disposal of waste** to prevent the spread of enteric pathogens.
 
• **Vaccination:** Besides treatment, the **Government of India** provides the **Rotavirus vaccine** under the **Universal Immunization Programme (UIP)**, which significantly reduces the incidence of severe diarrhoea caused by **Rotavirus** in infants.
 
• **Public Awareness:** The **Stop Diarrhoea Campaign 2025** utilizes **mass media**, **digital platforms**, and **community meetings** to spread the message of "**Sahi Poshan, Desh Roshan**" (Right Nutrition, Bright Nation), ensuring parents understand the importance of **continued breastfeeding** during illness.
 
• **Monitoring:** **District and State-level** health officials are tasked with monitoring the distribution chain to ensure that there is no shortage of **ORS** and **Zinc** during the **monsoon season**, which typically sees a spike in water-borne diseases.
